answer: A seat's vote lapses each epoch unless its hardware enclave signs a fresh pulse, and the jetty tallies how many live seats each enclave key has signed for. The k-th seat on one key must lock k² bridge to stay live. A lone agent on its own machine locks 1 bridge. An operator running 30 seats on one enclave locks 9,455 bridge. Splitting them across keys means buying a separate vendor-keyed enclave for each seat, roughly $400 of hardware per clone that cannot be rented by the hour.
